license_assessment: BSD-style three-clause permissive license; preserve exact supplied text
license_obligations: Retain copyright, conditions and disclaimer in source redistributions.
Reproduce copyright, conditions and disclaimer in binary distribution documentation/materials.
Do not use contributor names to endorse derived products without prior written permission.
runtime_use: ProjectStore imports atomic_save for complete single-file JSON, text, and JSONL replacements; eval.py uses atomic_save(overwrite=False) for new benchmark evidence and scoring sheets. ProjectStore recovery calls sync_directory before retiring its bounded intent. Locking and confinement are caller responsibilities.
upstream_package_build_dependency: flit_core >=3.2,<4 (not needed by this extracted runtime)
modifications: Retain complete original source copyright/license header and adapted AtomicSaver context-manager/publication structure.
Replace deterministic destination.part and user-selected part paths with fixed-size randomized same-directory .novel-*.tmp names; retry exclusive collisions without touching the prior entry.
Keep exclusive/no-follow creation and add close-on-exec flags where available; default new files to 0600 filtered by umask, without copying destination permissions.
Use Python os.replace for overwrite and os.link+unlink for no-clobber; no unsafe hard-link fallback or legacy ctypes branches.
Explicit UTF-8 and LF for requested text mode; binary remains default.
Clean owned descriptors and part files for setup/body/flush/fsync/close/publication failures without masking the first exception.
Attempt POSIX parent-directory fsync after publication. Report unsupported directory sync via directory_synced=False; propagate other postcommit errors without a rollback promise.
Remove overwrite_part, rm_part_on_exc and custom part names; reject context reuse; do not add file locking, directory creation, or confinement to this narrow kernel.
Expose sync_directory(path) so callers can resync already-published entries before bounded recovery retirement and sync intent deletion afterward.
honest_limits: One file is published at a time; there is no multi-file transaction or write lock.
Callers must confine destination/parent paths and protect read-modify-write operations.
A postpublication exception can leave the complete new file visible; actual readback is required to establish the current version.
Directory fsync is unavailable on non-POSIX hosts and can be unsupported by a filesystem; no universal power-loss durability guarantee.
SIGKILL/process loss can leave an unreferenced private temporary file; randomized names permit subsequent writes without unsafe stale-file deletion.
Atomic no-clobber fails closed when hard links are unsupported.
Upstream has only one directly targeted AtomicSaver PathLike smoke test in test_fileutils.py; Novel adds synthetic fault-injection coverage.
